question: What is the total sum of the exterior angles of any polygon, one at each vertex?

options.text: Depends on the number of sides

solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

A fundamental property of any convex polygon is that a full trip around its perimeter involves exactly one complete rotation.

Therefore, the total sum of all exterior angles, taking one at each vertex, is equivalent to one full circle.

One complete circle rotation is always equal to 360°.

**∴ The correct answer is 360°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Any arbitrary polygon with n sides.

**Formula Used:**

Sum of interior angles of an n-sided polygon = (n − 2) × 180°

At any vertex, Interior Angle + Exterior Angle = 180° (Linear Pair)

 Sum of exterior angles = 360°

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total sum of all interior and exterior angles for n vertices = n × 180°

⇒ Sum of exterior angles = Total sum − Sum of interior angles

⇒ Sum of exterior angles = n × 180° − (n − 2) × 180°

⇒ Sum of exterior angles = 180° × (n − n + 2)

⇒ Sum of exterior angles = 180° × 2 = 360°

⇒ The sum evaluates to 360° independent of the number of sides.

**∴ The correct answer is 360°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Interior Angles of a Polygon

The sum of interior angles of an n-sided polygon is defined as (n − 2) × 180°. For a regular polygon, each interior angle is equal to ((n − 2) × 180°) ÷ n.

Exterior Angles of a Regular Polygon

Since the total sum of exterior angles is always fixed at 360°, each exterior angle of an n-sided regular polygon is given exactly by 360° ÷ n.

Number of Diagonals

The total number of unique diagonals that can be drawn within an n-sided polygon is calculated using the formula n(n − 3) ÷ 2.
